title: Opinionated exception adapters and developer-facing remediation messages for SDKs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Provide an opinionated, cross-language exception adapter layer that presents actionable, localizable remediation messages and machine-readable error metadata to SDK consumers while preserving raw provider codes for observability and debugging. This ticket delivers API ergonomics and example usage for Python/TypeScript/Go, plus a migration path and telemetry schema.

Background: SDK teams have iterated on error mappings independently. Customers repeatedly ask for: (1) clear guidance on whether an error is transient/retryable, (2) exact recommended next steps (eg. backoff, decrease batch size, reissue with idempotency key), (3) streaming resume primitives, and (4) telemetry tokens to correlate SDK events with server-side traces. Previous efforts produced many similar ideas but inconsistent surface area across languages.

Scope: Build an "exception adapter" that wraps runtime errors into a standardized envelope with: code (short machine token), category (transient|terminal|client|auth|quota|rate_limit), retry_hint (none|idempotent|backoff|resume), human_message (short actionable sentence), long_help_link (doc URL), resume_token (optional, base64), and diagnostic_ids (list). Implement the adapter in Python/TS/Go idiomatically and include idiomatic examples and migration helpers. Ensure SDKs emit structured telemetry with error_code and retry_hint fields.

Out-of-scope: full server-side error cataloging and exhaustive mapping of every upstream code. We'll provide a recommended mapping and hooks to extend mappings per product integration.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Python, TS, Go) expose an ExceptionAdapter/convert_error function that returns the standardized envelope
Envelope fields: code, category, retry_hint, human_message, long_help_link, resume_token (optional), diagnostic_ids (list) are present and documented
Examples for streaming: client can resume with resume_token returned in error envelope and SDK provides an ergonomic resume helper
Telemetry: SDKs emit error_code and retry_hint as part of error events to our analytics backend (schema agreed)
Backward compatibility: existing error types remain available; adapter is opt-in by default for minor release, opt-out flag for customers
Integration tests: unit tests that simulate transient vs terminal errors and assert retry_hint semantics across languages
Docs: migration guide + troubleshooting page with repair recipes and sample git PR for each SDK
design_notes: We use an opinionated envelope rather than changing server APIs: adapter maps server error payloads to the envelope in-client so rollout can be SDK-driven
Codes are short machine tokens (eg. ERR_RATE_LIMIT, ERR_MISSING_KEY). We keep original server_code in diagnostic_ids so engineers can look up exact server-side semantics.
Categories are used by higher-level SDK helpers (auto-retry layer, backoff module, resume middleware) to make deterministic decisions.

retry_hint semantics: 'idempotent' means safe immediate retry if request was idempotent; 'backoff' means wait exponential backoff then retry; 'resume' used only for streaming resumable errors with token payload.
Resume token shape: base64 JSON that includes session_id and sequence_cursor. Tokens are opaque to users but SDKs provide helpers to attach them when resuming streams.
Human messages are concise, localized strings (EN by default) with a long_help_link pointing to a doc containing troubleshooting recipes. Messages should not leak internals or PII.
We will not force automatic retries by default for user-initiated requests. High-level helpers (eg. .with_retries()) opt into adapter-driven behavior.

Telemetry: include error.envelope.code, error.envelope.retry_hint, error.envelope.category, error.diagnostic_ids, span_id, and request_id. Use existing telemetry pipeline keys to avoid schema churn (coordinate with Observability).
implementation_plan: API design: finalize envelope fields and name conventions; land a short interface spec (this ticket)
Python: implement ExceptionAdapter class and helpers in redwood_sdk.errors; add a convenience decorator @with_error_adapter to convert thrown errors
TypeScript: provide function adaptError(err) returning ErrorEnvelope and a middleware for streaming clients to populate resume_token
Go: implement AdaptError(err error) (ErrorEnvelope, bool) pattern and provide ResumeToken type and helper functions
Tests: create unit tests that assert mapping for simulated server payloads: 429 -> RATE_LIMIT/backoff; 401 -> auth/terminal; connection reset during stream -> resume
Docs: write migration guide + examples + long_help_link troubleshooting page (Confluence/Docs site).
Examples + snippets: three language-specific code examples demonstrating inspecting retry_hint and resuming streams
Telemetry: add event fields to SDK telemetry library and validate in dev staging with sample events
Rollout: alpha behind feature flag for early integrators, beta in next minor release opt-in, GA default opt-out for existing users (to avoid breaking behavior)
python_snippet:
from redwood_sdk import Client, errors

client = Client()
try:
    resp = client.generate(prompt="hello")
except Exception as exc:
    envelope = errors.ExceptionAdapter.adapt(exc)
    # envelope.code, envelope.retry_hint, envelope.human_message are available
    print(envelope.human_message)
    if envelope.retry_hint == 'backoff':
        # use SDK backoff helper
        client.with_retries(max_attempts=3).generate(prompt="hello")
testing_plan: Unit tests for adapter mapping covering at least 12 canonical server payload shapes (rate limit, quota, auth, bad_request, stream_checkpoint, connection_reset)
Integration test in staging that forces a streaming interruption and validates resume_token roundtrip between client and server mocks
Fuzz tests for resume_token expiry and malformed token handling
Telemetry validation: assert error.envelope fields appear in events in the observability staging dataset
Cross-language contract tests: one canonical JSON error payload consumed by Python/TS/Go adapters should produce equivalent envelope fields
rollout_plan: Week 1 (alpha): feature-flagged release to internal teams and 2 partner customers. Collect integration feedback and telemetry.
Week 3 (beta): enable opt-in adapter in public SDK minors; publish migration guide and examples; begin doc long_help_link population
Week 6 (GA candidate): default opt-in for new SDK installs; existing installs keep prior behavior unless they opt into adapter
Deprecation: after 3 months of GA, announce deprecation timeline for legacy unstructured SDK errors with a 6-month opt-out window for large customers
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: adapter could change consumable error semantics and break customers relying on exact exception types. Mitigation: opt-in rollout, compatibility tests, and conversion helpers that preserve original exception on envelope as diagnostic_id.
Risk: resume_token misuse may leak session semantics. Mitigation: tokens are opaque and short-lived; SDKs validate and refuse expired tokens with clear human_message.
Risk: telemetry schema changes. Mitigation: reuse existing telemetry keys and coordinate with Observability before shipping.
